why: Top k by a key: count frequencies, then keep a min-heap of size k keyed by (frequency, tie-break). The heap root is the weakest of the current top k, so each new candidate either replaces it or is discarded.
hints: First turn the array into (value, frequency) pairs. Now it is 'the k best pairs'.
Keep only k pairs in a min-heap ordered so the root is the worst of them: (frequency, -value) makes lower frequency, then larger value, the worst. Replace the root whenever a better pair comes.
Counter, then heappush / heapreplace: O(d log k) for d distinct values. Sort the k survivors best first for the output. (Bucket sort by frequency is the O(n) alternative.)
pitfalls: The tie rule (smaller value first) must be built into the heap key, not patched afterwards.
Sorting all distinct values is O(d log d); fine here, but the point is the size-k heap.
